_comment: The build the autododge research was verified against. This is a RECORD, not a policy: Fingerprint.ps1 compares the installed game against these values and refuses on mismatch. Regenerate after every game or runtime update, and record what changed.

game.note: Two apphosts ship with DIFFERENT builds of the game assembly. The root exe is the SharpDX/DirectX one (includes Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App); OpenGL\DarzasDominion.exe is the MonoGame one and carries its own runtime copy. Only the root one has been analysed.

assembly.note: ILONLY must be set and ManagedNativeHeader must be 0. If the assembly ever ships ReadyToRun, a compileMethod hook stops seeing its methods and the whole hook design needs rework. The SHA-256 is checked because size alone does not detect an edit that preserves length -- a mutation test proved that gap: flipping one byte of the assembly left the size check passing.

runtime.note: TieredCompilation MUST be false. It is the single assumption the hook design rests on: with it off, each method is JIT-compiled once and a detour is permanent. A future patch flipping it to true invalidates the approach unless DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0 is forced in the launcher environment.

jit.note: Verified by disassembly of the shipped clrjit.dll. getVersionIdentifier is at slot 2 on .NET 5+; the widely-copied community JIT-hook libraries hardcode slot 4, which was correct only up to .NET Core 3.1. compileMethod has always been slot 0. Read slot 2 and validate the returned GUID rather than trusting any hardcoded index.

targetMethods._comment: The four primary detour targets, by IL hash (to be filled by tools/il_index.py, Phase 0). Absent until the table is generated; Fingerprint.ps1 reports this as a known gap rather than a failure.
